answer: A memory-hard proof-of-work handshake forces each agent to solve memory-bound puzzles before peer admission. An attacker incurs the verifiable electricity and hardware cost of dedicated memory per identity. Refusing to harbor unvetted nodes prevents a vast nebula of automated clones from disguising collusion behind a velvet facade of normal traffic. A key limitation is that well-resourced adversaries can still finance hardware clusters to mint multiple identities.
